tasks.title: Hand-author RED oracle test_source_qualify_gate.py covering GO, every UNKNOWN, and every SKIP gate
acceptance_criteria: Includes one GO all-pass case asserting decision 'GO', reason 'qualified', and the exact target_spec contents.
Includes one UNKNOWN case per missing required key (expected_payout, open_submissions, days_since_audit, fp_risk), each asserting reason 'missing key: <name>' and target_spec None.

Includes one SKIP case per failing gate asserting the exact reason string: 'expected_payout <= 0', 'open_submissions >= saturation_cap (50)', 'days_since_audit < freshness_min (7)', and 'fp_risk match'.
The oracle is non-vacuous and RED against the declared mutant of ngv2.source_qualify_gate (fails when the module's decision logic is mutated).

spec.objective: Provide a committed, non-vacuous, hand-authored RED oracle that pins the exact GO/SKIP/UNKNOWN contract of qualify(), including every reason string and the GO target_spec, so any weakening or reordering of the gate logic fails the test.
functional_requirements: Import qualify from ngv2.source_qualify_gate and exercise it directly with in-memory dicts.
Assert a GO all-pass case returns decision 'GO', reason 'qualified', and target_spec equal to {'repo': ..., 'package': ..., 'expected_payout': ...} matching the inputs.
Assert UNKNOWN for missing expected_payout with reason 'missing key: expected_payout' and target_spec None.
Assert UNKNOWN for missing open_submissions with reason 'missing key: open_submissions' and target_spec None.
Assert UNKNOWN for missing days_since_audit with reason 'missing key: days_since_audit' and target_spec None.
Assert UNKNOWN for missing fp_risk with reason 'missing key: fp_risk' and target_spec None.
Assert SKIP for expected_payout <= 0 with reason 'expected_payout <= 0' and target_spec None.
Assert SKIP for open_submissions >= saturation_cap with reason 'open_submissions >= saturation_cap (50)' and target_spec None.
Assert SKIP for days_since_audit < freshness_min with reason 'days_since_audit < freshness_min (7)' and target_spec None.
Assert SKIP for fp_risk True with reason 'fp_risk match' and target_spec None.
spec.interfaces: pytest test module importing ngv2.source_qualify_gate.qualify; pure assertions on the returned dict, no fixtures touching IO.
edge_cases: GO case must use a payload that passes ALL four gates so that target_spec is asserted on a genuinely qualified target.
Each UNKNOWN case drops exactly one required key, leaving the others valid, to prove first-missing-key naming.
Each SKIP case violates exactly one gate while keeping prior gates passing, to prove the named gate is the first failure.
Use default saturation_cap=50 and freshness_min=7 so the asserted reason strings contain (50) and (7).
non_goals: Integration is explicitly out of scope: no integration_test is expected; the FSM integration of this verdict is delivered separately by ngv2_lifecycle_fsm_wiring.
Do NOT exercise any real bounty-platform client, network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness; oracle_result is supplied inline as the injected seam's output.
Do NOT test or trigger any FSM transition or wiring.
Do NOT weaken assertions to accommodate alternate reason strings.
spec.implementation_notes: One test function (or parametrization) per case. Build a baseline valid target and oracle_result, then derive each variant by mutating one field or dropping one key. Assert on the full returned dict where practical (decision, reason, target_spec) so a mutant that swaps decisions or reasons is caught. This is a RED oracle: it is expected to fail until source_qualify_gate_impl is correct, and must fail against the module's declared mutant.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Inline target dicts {repo, package} and oracle_result dicts with required keys {expected_payout, open_submissions, days_since_audit, fp_risk}; a fully-qualifying baseline plus one-key-dropped and one-gate-violated variants, all using default saturation_cap=50 and freshness_min=7.

token_budget_ratio.note: Test-only deliverable (RED oracle); no production code, so all budget is test tokens.

tasks.title: Implement pure ngv2/source_qualify_gate.py qualify() returning GO/SKIP/UNKNOWN
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/source_qualify_gate.py exposes qualify(target: dict, oracle_result: dict, *, saturation_cap: int = 50, freshness_min: int = 7) -> dict.

Returns {'decision': 'UNKNOWN', 'reason': 'missing key: <name>', 'target_spec': None} when oracle_result lacks any of the four required keys, naming the FIRST missing key in the canonical order expected_payout, open_submissions, days_since_audit, fp_risk.

Returns {'decision': 'GO', 'reason': 'qualified', 'target_spec': {...}} iff expected_payout > 0 AND open_submissions < saturation_cap AND days_since_audit >= freshness_min AND fp_risk is False; target_spec echoes the qualified target (repo, package, expected_payout).

Returns {'decision': 'SKIP', 'reason': '<failing gate>', 'target_spec': None} naming the FIRST failing gate among 'expected_payout <= 0', 'open_submissions >= saturation_cap (<cap>)', 'days_since_audit < freshness_min (<min>)', 'fp_risk match'.
saturation_cap and freshness_min are tunable keyword args defaulting to 50 and 7 and their concrete values are interpolated into the relevant SKIP reason strings.
Module is pure, total, deterministic, side-effect-free, and imports only stdlib and ngv2 (e.g. ngv2.contracts); no network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness.
No silent SKIP: every non-GO, non-UNKNOWN result carries a reason naming the failing gate.

spec.objective: Port the GO/SKIP/UNKNOWN decision behavior of legacy bounty_gate.py + qualify_target.py into a single pure, stdlib+ngv2-only, deterministic, total module ngv2/source_qualify_gate.py exposing qualify(target, oracle_result, *, saturation_cap=50, freshness_min=7).
functional_requirements: Expose a function qualify(target: dict, oracle_result: dict, *, saturation_cap: int = 50, freshness_min: int = 7) -> dict returning a dict with keys decision, reason, target_spec.

When oracle_result lacks any of the four required keys (expected_payout, open_submissions, days_since_audit, fp_risk), return decision 'UNKNOWN' with reason 'missing key: <name>' for the FIRST missing key in that canonical order and target_spec None.

When all four required keys are present and expected_payout > 0 AND open_submissions < saturation_cap AND days_since_audit >= freshness_min AND fp_risk is False, return decision 'GO' with reason 'qualified' and target_spec echoing the qualified target as {'repo': target['repo'], 'package': target['package'], 'expected_payout': oracle_result['expected_payout']}.

When keys are present but the GO conjunction does not hold, return decision 'SKIP' with reason naming the FIRST failing gate evaluated in order: 'expected_payout <= 0', then 'open_submissions >= saturation_cap (<cap>)', then 'days_since_audit < freshness_min (<min>)', then 'fp_risk match'; target_spec None.
Interpolate the concrete saturation_cap and freshness_min argument values into the saturation and freshness SKIP reason strings respectively.
Keep the function pure, total, deterministic, and side-effect-free, importing only stdlib and ngv2 modules (no network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, randomness, or filesystem writes).
spec.interfaces: qualify(target: dict, oracle_result: dict, *, saturation_cap: int = 50, freshness_min: int = 7) -> dict; returns {'decision': 'GO'|'SKIP'|'UNKNOWN', 'reason': str, 'target_spec': dict|None}.
edge_cases: oracle_result missing multiple required keys: name only the first in canonical order expected_payout, open_submissions, days_since_audit, fp_risk.
Boundary expected_payout == 0 fails the > 0 gate and yields SKIP 'expected_payout <= 0'.
Boundary open_submissions == saturation_cap fails the < saturation_cap gate (>= is the SKIP condition).
Boundary days_since_audit == freshness_min passes the >= freshness_min gate (not a SKIP).

fp_risk truthy-but-not-True (e.g. 1) still triggers 'fp_risk match' since the GO requires fp_risk is False; ensure the gate is 'fp_risk is not False' rather than identity to True only — match the brief's fp_risk is False requirement.
Multiple gates failing simultaneously: only the FIRST in evaluation order is reported.
Non-default saturation_cap/freshness_min values are reflected in the reason strings.
non_goals: Integration is explicitly out of scope: this is a pure, total, side-effect-free function tested in isolation; no integration_test is expected because the FSM integration of this verdict is delivered separately by ngv2_lifecycle_fsm_wiring.
Do NOT implement the real side-effecting bounty-platform client, network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness; the bounty_oracle producing oracle_result is an injected seam, not built here.
Do NOT perform any FSM transition or wiring.
Do NOT weaken any admitting criterion (the GO conjunction and gate ordering are fixed).
spec.implementation_notes:
Define a tuple of required keys in canonical order and iterate to find the first missing one for the UNKNOWN branch. Then evaluate the four gates in the documented order, returning SKIP on the first failure with the interpolated cap/min values. Only after all gates pass, build the GO target_spec from target['repo'], target['package'], and oracle_result['expected_payout']. Consume ngv2.contracts if it defines the decision/result shapes or key names; otherwise keep dependencies to stdlib only. Keep no module-level mutable state.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: In-memory target dicts ({repo, package}) and oracle_result dicts with the four required keys; variants that drop exactly one required key, that violate exactly one gate, and that violate multiple gates to assert first-failure ordering; plus non-default saturation_cap/freshness_min values.

token_budget_ratio.note: Small pure decision module; tests dominate to lock the exact reason strings and gate ordering.
